Q: Can we automate Apple App Store Connect app update with "Whats New" localization? A:

Yes, you can automate updating the “What’s New” localization in App Store Connect.

There are two main approaches:

1. Using Fastlane (recommended)

Fastlane’s deliver supports localized release notes via the metadata folder structure.

Example structure:

fastlane/metadata/
  en-US/release_notes.txt
  de-DE/release_notes.txt
  fr-FR/release_notes.txt

Then run:

fastlane deliver --metadata_path ./fastlane/metadata

This will upload localized “What’s New” text along with the build.

2. Using App Store Connect API

You can programmatically update appStoreVersionLocalizations via the App Store Connect API.

The endpoint allows PATCH requests to update whatsNew per locale once you authenticate using an API key.

If you're trying to streamline release note management across versions and locales, it helps to structure them separately from your CI pipeline and generate them dynamically before upload.

Q: Using R to count instances of strings where the order of the letters isn't important A:

As @Rui Barradas mentioned, you could first make the sequence sorted and then apply table.

My solution follows the same idea but use order + intToUtf8 + utf8ToInt to finish the sorting processes

x <-c("AB", "Ab", "aB", "ab")
y <-c("AB", "Ab", "aB", "ab")

table(outer(x,y, Vectorize(\(p,q) {u <- paste0(p,q); intToUtf8(utf8ToInt(u)[order(utf8ToInt(u))])})))

and you will obtain

aabb Aabb AAbb AABb AABB ABab ABBa Baab BBaa 
   1    2    1    2    1    4    2    2    1

Q: Django date validation, help needed A:

use "clean()" instead of "save()", bacuase the pipeline of django models is:

  1. It calls form.is_valid()

  2. That calls model.full_clean()

  3. That calls clean()

so the code would be sth like:

from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.db import models

class Semester(models.Model):
    start_date = models.DateField()
    end_date = models.DateField()

    def clean(self):
        if self.end_date <= self.start_date:
            raise ValidationError({
                'end_date': "End date must be after start date."
            })

Q: Set password for VM users when OS Login is enabled: Authentication token manipulation error A:

Came across this issue on some GCP vms running as jenkins agents, controller was unable to launch ssh session, turned out the password expiry date was the issue.
Since the jenkins user on those VMs has no password, but /etc/shadow was still setting a max of 365 days for password expiry that was triggering the reset password and this was failing.
As I didn't want to set a password for the jenkins user any way, I updated the max amount of days that the password is valid field in /etc/shadow to never expire a.k.a 99999
# chage -M 99999 jenkins

Q: Why am I receiving emails with a specific List-Unsubscribe header even though I never subscribed? A:

You need to show us the full detailed headers of a couple of sample emails (munging your own email identity). The image you shared provides no insight at all into what is going on.

Most likely you have clicked on something somewhere or used your email address on a vendor site that has been scraped or a friends computer infected with malware. Flagging them as spam in your mail client will probably get rid of them or you could add a custom rule to recognise them and dump them into the bin.
